Approval(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when the allowance of a `spender` for an `owner` is set by a call to {approve}. `value` is the new allowance.

Initialized(uint8).details: Triggered when the contract has been initialized or reinitialized.

Paused(address).details: Emitted when the pause is triggered by `account`.

Transfer(address,address,uint256).details: Emitted when `value` tokens are moved from one account (`from`) to another (`to`). Note that `value` may be zero.

Unpaused(address).details: Emitted when the pause is lifted by `account`.

params.accounts: Accounts to mark as permanently exempt (cannot have transfers blocked)

approve(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-approve}. NOTE: If `amount` is the maximum `uint256`, the allowance is not updated on `transferFrom`. This is semantically equivalent to an infinite approval. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

blockUserTransfers(address[]).details: Re-applying the block before expiry refreshes the hold to `block.timestamp + 1 days`      (i.e. not cumulative; never more than 24h from the latest call). Exempt addresses cannot be blocked.      Emits {UserTransfersBlocked} only when the timestamp changes.

params.amount: the amount of rsETH to burn

decimals().details: Returns the number of decimals used to get its user representation. For example, if `decimals` equals `2`, a balance of `505` tokens should be displayed to a user as `5.05` (`505 / 10 ** 2`). Tokens usually opt for a value of 18, imitating the relationship between Ether and Wei. This is the default value returned by this function, unless it's overridden. NOTE: This information is only used for _display_ purposes: it in no way affects any of the arithmetic of the contract, including {IERC20-balanceOf} and {IERC20-transfer}.

decreaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically decreases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address. - `spender` must have allowance for the caller of at least `subtractedValue`.

returns._0: uint256 The start timestamp of the effective current 24-hour period

getNextDailyLimitResetTimestamp().details: A mint executed at exactly this timestamp is counted towards the next period's minting limit

returns._0: uint256 The timestamp at which the effective current minting period ends

increaseAllowance(address,uint256).details: Atomically increases the allowance granted to `spender` by the caller. This is an alternative to {approve} that can be used as a mitigation for problems described in {IERC20-approve}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. Requirements: - `spender` cannot be the zero address.

params.amount: the amount of rsETH to mint

name().details: Returns the name of the token.

pause().details: Triggers stopped state. Contract must not be paused.

paused().details: Returns true if the contract is paused, and false otherwise.

recoverFrozenFunds(address).details: Only callable by LRT admin. Works only while the block is active.      Emits {FrozenFundsRecovered} even if the recovered amount is zero (for transparency and completeness).

params._custodyAddress: The custody address for recovered funds

returns._0: uint256 The remaining daily minting limit

params._maxMintAmountPerDay: The maximum amount that can be minted in 24 hours

symbol().details: Returns the symbol of the token, usually a shorter version of the name.

transfer(address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transfer}. Requirements: - `to` cannot be the zero address. - the caller must have a balance of at least `amount`.

transferFrom(address,address,uint256).details: See {IERC20-transferFrom}. Emits an {Approval} event indicating the updated allowance. This is not required by the EIP. See the note at the beginning of {ERC20}. NOTE: Does not update the allowance if the current allowance is the maximum `uint256`. Requirements: - `from` and `to` cannot be the zero address. - `from` must have a balance of at least `amount`. - the caller must have allowance for ``from``'s tokens of at least `amount`.

unpause().details: Returns to normal state. Contract must be paused.

isPermanentlyExempt.details: Permanently exempt addresses mapping (rsETH transfers for these can never be blocked)

transfersBlockedUntil.details: If > 0, transfers TO or FROM this address are blocked until timestamp (24h block)

addPermanentExemptions(address[]).notice: Permanently add accounts to the exempted list (non-reversible)

blockUserTransfers(address[]).notice: Block transfers TO and FROM given users for 24 hours

burnFrom(address,uint256).notice: Burns rsETH when called by an authorized caller

currentPeriodMintedAmount().notice: Amount minted in the current 24-hour period

custodyAddress().notice: Address to which recovered funds are sent

getCurrentPeriodStartTime().notice: Returns the aligned start timestamp of the effective current 24-hour minting period, accounting for any possibly skipped days

getNextDailyLimitResetTimestamp().notice: Returns the timestamp at which the current effective daily minting period ends, accounting for any skipped days during which no minting occurred

maxMintAmountPerDay().notice: Maximum amount that can be minted in a 24-hour period

mint(address,uint256).notice: Mints rsETH when called by an authorized caller

periodStartTime().notice: Start time of the current 24-hour period

recoverFrozenFunds(address).notice: Recover the entire balance from a currently blocked, non-exempt address to a designated custody address

reinitialize(uint256,address).notice: Initializes the contract with a period start time and the custody address

remainingDailyMintLimit().notice: Gets the remaining daily minting limit

setCustodyAddress(address).notice: Sets the custody address for recovered funds

setMaxMintAmountPerDay(uint256).notice: Sets the maximum amount that can be minted in 24 hours

userdoc.notice: The ERC20 contract for the rsETH token
